Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 1998) 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
SEAMLESS ALUMINIUM BOTTLES 

( First Revision ) 



E 
o 
o 

_Q 
CO 



1. Scope — Prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for seamless aluminium 
bottles up to 1 000 ml capacity. 

2. Terminology — For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 1394-1984 'Glossary 
of terms relating to metal containers ( third revision )' shall apply. 

3. Capacity — The nominal filling capacities of the aluminium bottles shall be 25, 50, 100, 200, 500 
and 1 000 ml. 

4. Requirements 

4.1 Pattern — The bottles shall have a plain neck and bulged in bottom as shown in Fig. 1. Alternate 
types of neck design as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer may be provided. 

4.2 Dimensions and Tolerances — The bottles shall be manufactured to the dimensions as shown in 
Fig. 1. 

4.3 Material— The bottles shall be made from aluminium alloy conforming to Grade 19000, 19500 
or 31000 of IS : 737-1974 'Specification for wrought aluminium alleys, sheet and strip (for general 
engineering purposes ) ( second revision )'. 

4.4 Manufacture — The bottles shall be of seamless construction as shown in Fig. 1. The bottles 
shall be in a clean condition, free of scratches and dents. If agreed to between the purchaser and the 
supplier, the bottles may be given a suitable protective external decorative coating. 

4.5 Air Pressure Test — The bottles, when subject to internal air pressure of 50 kPa ( ss 050 kgf/cm 2 ) 
for 15 seconds, shall not show any sign of leakage when immersed in water. The test shall be carried 
out as prescribed in 3 of IS : 2471-1963 'Methods of test for metal containers'. 

5. Marking — The bottles shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized 

trade-mark, if any. 

5.1 Standard Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

6. Sampling — Representative samples of the containers for tests shall be drawn as prescribed in 
IS : 3259-1966 'Methods for sampling of metal containers'. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

Seamless aluminium bottles are used in large quantities for packing of natural and synthetic 
perfumery materials like sandalwood oil and essences used in food and beverages industry. This 
standard, first published in 1966, has been revised to update it with respect to the mateial requirements 
and dimensional tolerances according to the present manufacturing practice in the country.
